acceptedAnswer.text: The Pair is a free, open-source AI pair programming desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. It runs two AI coding agents on one task, a read-only Mentor and an Executor, so the work is planned, implemented, tested, and reviewed by separate roles instead of one model checking itself.

mainEntity.name: How is The Pair different from Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or Aider?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Aider drive a single assistant that writes code and reviews its own output. The Pair is a Cursor and Copilot alternative that separates the two jobs: the Executor changes code and runs commands, and a read-only Mentor, which can be a different model, plans the work and reviews every result before it is accepted.

mainEntity.name: Which AI models does The Pair support?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any model reachable through an endpoint you connect, including GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, GLM, Qwen, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek, plus local models via Ollama. The Pair speaks four wire protocols (OpenAI Chat, Anthropic, Responses and Command Code). Endpoints can be imported from the configuration of opencode, codex, claude, kimi, pi, omp, gemini or killi, added by hand with a base URL and API key, or signed in with a ChatGPT, Command Code, OpenCode Go or Muse Code subscription. Mentor and Executor can use different models.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Claude Code, Codex or another agent CLI installed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Since version 3.0 The Pair talks to model endpoints directly over HTTPS and runs the agents' tools (read, write, edit, bash, grep, glob) itself, scoped to the pair's workspace. It needs one model endpoint with a credential and nothing else.

mainEntity.name: How does The Pair reduce AI coding hallucinations?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Pair reduces AI coding hallucinations by splitting the workflow into two roles. The Executor writes and verifies code, while the read-only Mentor reads the diff, runs acceptance checks such as tests and lint, and returns a verdict with risk, evidence and a next step. Work that fails the review goes back for another iteration instead of being accepted.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the agents get stuck or the app closes mid-run?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Pair warns after 120 seconds without agent output and marks the agent stalled after 600 seconds. An optional per-pair iteration cap pauses the run for human review when it is reached. Session snapshots are saved as the run goes, so an interrupted session is offered back on the next launch with its conversation history and turn state.
